240	But the Ari once slept, on Parashat Balak, a midday nap, a few minutes, I know, and then he began to mumble
241	something.
242	Rabbi Chaim Vital was so excited that he put his ear inside the mouth of the Ari to hear what he was saying.
243	So the Ari said, what is your ear doing
244	inside my mouth?
245	He told him, Rabbi, I wanted to hear what you speak when you sleep.
246	He said to him, believe me, even if I sat with you now and explained everything they taught me,
247	80 years, a veteran student, I wouldn't manage to explain what they taught me just now in five minutes
248	in Heaven.
249	80 years, a veteran student, on the secret of Bilaam's donkey, that is what he tells him.
250	80 years.
251	So of course, the sages of Israel and the great ones of Israel, and Rabbi Chaim Vital was a genius of the world.
252	He was a genius of the world, he was Rabbi Chaim Vital, a student of Rabbi Moshe Alshich, Rabbi Moshe Alshich was a student of
253	Rabbi Yosef Karo, Rabbi Yosef Karo was ordained by Maharí Beirav, Maharí Beirav wanted to do
254	the semichah, they lived in the time of Maharí Taitsak, do you know who Maharí Taitsak is?
255	Rabbi Yosef Taitsak, the Rav Chida writes in Shem HaGedolim, under Maharí Taitsak, Rabbi Yosef Taitsak, forty
256	years he did not sleep on a bed, and he learned without a break, and only put his head on
257	the lectern, forty years he did not taste the taste of, of course, a bed.
258	Well, what?
259	They were giants of the world.
260	Maharí Beirav ordained Rabbi Yosef Karo, with the well-known controversy with the Maharalbach.
261	The Maharalbach did not agree to the semichah, but in the end Maharí Beirav thought that if all the sages of Israel
262	truly want to ordain, they can renew the semichah.
263	The Kadosh Baruch Hu, so to speak, placed His hands on Moshe, Moshe placed his hands on Yehoshua, Yehoshua placed his
264	hands on the elders, the elders on the prophets, each sage placed his hands on the other sages, this is called
265	semichah, and this is called a true rabbi, who is ordained by one who was ordained by one who was ordained by one, all the way to
266	the halachah given to Moshe at Sinai. In truth, over the generations everything disappeared, and the sages already
267	in the Gemara, the Romans decreed that they not ordain, and if they ordained, they would be killed, and so died
268	some of the sages of Israel who were caught ordaining and were killed, and in practice we are in exile,
269	this army, for two thousand years already, and we were poured from vessel to vessel and almost none of us remained, so writes
270	the Rav Beit Yosef in his introduction to the Beit Yosef.
271	It is like you take water, pour it into another vessel, take water, pour into another vessel, a little remains in each vessel, almost nothing
272	remains in the last vessel.
273	The last cup is already a quarter, a quarter of a cup.
274	There was a whole cup, nothing was spilled, but from vessel to vessel you pass from Modena to Italy, from Italy to Spain,
275	from Spain to Turkey, to Izmir, to Constantinople.
276	All this you leave behind you, the journey, the wandering takes away from your strength, from your abilities, from your money,
277	as Rashi says in the Parashah, "Lech Lecha, from your land," you lose some of your strength, so in the end
278	the semichah ceased, they no longer ordain.
